name: @mthines/reaper-mcp

tools.name: get_project_info
tools.description: Get current REAPER project info: name, track count, tempo, time signature, sample rate, transport state

tools.name: undo_project
tools.description: Undo the last undo point in the REAPER project (any edit, including ones made by these tools) and report its label, plus the next undo/redo labels.

tools.name: redo_project
tools.description: Redo the last undone edit in the REAPER project and report its label, plus the next undo/redo labels.

tools.name: save_project
tools.description: Save the REAPER project. Without a path, saves it where it already lives. With path (an absolute .rpp file in an existing directory) it writes a copy there: the open project keeps its own path (savedAsCopy: true), so a never-saved project stays unsaved. Never opens a dialog: a never-saved project without path is refused; an existing different file is refused unless overwrite is true.

path.description: Absolute .rpp path to write a copy to

overwrite.description: Replace an existing file at path

tools.name: get_render_settings
tools.description: Get the project render settings: output directory, file name pattern, format with its bit depth or MP3 bitrate, secondary format, source (master, stems, selected items, region matrix with its rows), bounds (custom/project/time_selection/…), custom start/end, sample rate (0 = project rate), channels, dither and noise shaping, loudness normalization and limiter, embedded metadata, and the target files a render would write.

tools.name: set_render_settings
tools.description: Set any of the project render settings; returns them as read back. All fields are validated before any is written, so an invalid request changes nothing. Covers what is rendered (source: master, stems of the selected tracks, master + stems, selected tracks via the master, the selected media items alone or through the master, the region render matrix), the encoding (bit depth, MP3 bitrate, dither), loudness normalization with a limiter, and embedded metadata.

filePattern.description: File name pattern without extension; REAPER wildcards like $project, $track, $region allowed

secondaryFormat.description: Second file written by the same render; none disables it

source.description: What is rendered: master mix; stems = one file per selected track (pick them with render_project tracks); master_and_stems; selected_via_master = the selected tracks through the master; region_matrix = the tracks set per region in regionMatrix (needs bounds all_regions or selected_regions); selected_items = one file per selected media item; selected_items_via_master = the selected items through the master (select them with set_selected_items)

regionMatrix.description: Region render matrix rows (source region_matrix); each listed region renders exactly these tracks

regionIndex.description: Region number as list_regions reports it

items.description: Track: 0-based index (-1 = master), exact name, "{GUID}", or "master". A digit string means a track name first, then the index.

tracks.description: Tracks this region renders: index, name, "{GUID}" or "master"; replaces the row

bitDepth.description: Bit depth of the primary format: wav 16/24/32/32f (float), aiff and flac 16/24

mp3Bitrate.description: MP3 constant bitrate in kbps (32-320); format must be mp3

dither.description: Dither the master and stems (use when reducing to 16 bit)

normalize.description: Normalize every rendered file to normalizeTarget by this measure

normalizeTarget.description: Normalize target in dB (LUFS for lufs_*; dBFS for peak/true_peak), -70 to 0

normalizeOnlyTooLoud.description: Only turn down files louder than the target

limitTruePeak.description: Limit on true peak instead of sample peak

metadata.description: Embedded metadata, written to ID3 (MP3), INFO/BWF/AXML (WAV) and Vorbis (FLAC/OGG) at once; "" clears a field. Turns embedding on

metadataRaw.description: Exact REAPER metadata keys, e.g. {"ID3:TCOM": "Composer"}; "" clears

embedMetadata.description: Embed the stored metadata in rendered files

tools.name: render_project
tools.description: Render the project with its current render settings (set them with set_render_settings) and return the files written, each measured: duration, integrated LUFS, true peak and sample peak. Synchronous: REAPER is busy until the render finishes, so keep renders short. Refused when a target file already exists (REAPER would ask) unless overwrite is true, when bounds is time_selection with no time selection, and when the format or secondary format is an encoder outside wav/aiff/flac/mp3/ogg/opus (they can open a dialog).

overwrite.description: Delete existing target files before rendering

tracks.description: For source stems / master_and_stems / selected_via_master: the tracks to render (index, name or "{GUID}"), selected for this render only

items.description: Track: 0-based index (-1 = master), exact name, "{GUID}", or "master". A digit string means a track name first, then the index.

analyze.description: Measure each file written (default true; up to 16 files)

tools.name: render_versions
tools.description: Render alternate versions in one call (instrumental, a cappella, TV mix, clean): for each version the listed tracks are muted on top of the current mutes, the file pattern gets "-<name>" (or the version's own filePattern), and the project renders with the current settings. Every track, name and target is checked before the first render; mutes and the file pattern are restored afterwards, also when a render fails. Each file comes back measured like render_project.

name.description: Version name, used in the file name: letters, digits, space, - _ .

mute.description: Tracks muted in this version (index, name, "{GUID}")

items.description: Track: 0-based index (-1 = master), exact name, "{GUID}", or "master". A digit string means a track name first, then the index.

filePattern.description: File pattern for this version instead of "<pattern>-<name>"

versions.description: The versions to render, in order

tools.name: get_project_settings
tools.description: Get project settings: path, sample rate and whether it is forced, title, author, notes, repeat (loop playback), and metronome (a global REAPER option).

tools.name: set_project_settings
tools.description: Set any of: sampleRate, useProjectSampleRate, title, author, notes, repeat, metronome. Returns the settings as read back. metronome is a global REAPER option (it is not stored in the project and undo does not revert it). Invalid values change nothing.

useProjectSampleRate.description: Force the project sample rate (may reconfigure the audio device)

repeat.description: Repeat / loop playback of the time selection

tools.name: list_tracks
tools.description: List tracks in the current REAPER project with name, index, volume, mute/solo state, and folder structure. In large sessions filter it: parent (a folder track — returns everything inside it), nameContains, compact (index, name, parentIndex, depth, volume, pan, mute, solo, fxCount only), offset/limit. With no params it returns every track as before; with any, it returns { total, offset, returned, hasMore, tracks }.

parent.description: Folder track (index or exact name) — return only the tracks inside it, at any depth

nameContains.description: Only tracks whose name contains this (case-insensitive)

compact.description: Only index, name, parentIndex, depth, volume, pan, mute, solo, fxCount

limit.description: Return at most this many tracks

tools.name: get_track_properties
tools.description: Get detailed properties of a specific track including volume, pan, mute, solo, and FX chain

tools.name: set_track_property
tools.description: Set a track property: volume (dB), pan (-1.0 to 1.0), mute/solo/recordArm/phase (0/1), input (REAPER input index), playOffsetMs (track playback offset in ms, negative = earlier; use with measure_track_alignment)

property.description: Property to set: volume (dB), pan (-1.0–1.0), mute/solo/recordArm/phase (0 or 1), input (REAPER input index, -1=no input), playOffsetMs (ms, -500..500)

value.description: Value: volume in dB, pan -1.0–1.0, mute/solo/recordArm/phase 0 or 1, input = REAPER input index

tools.name: add_fx
tools.description: Add an FX plugin to a track by name (e.g. "ReaEQ", "JS: Schwa's Spectral Analyzer", "VST: Pro-Q 3")

position.description: 0-based slot to insert at (0 = first); -1 or omit to append

tools.name: remove_fx
tools.description: Remove an FX plugin from a track by its index in the FX chain

fxIndex.description: Zero-based FX index in the chain

tools.name: get_fx_parameters
tools.description: List parameters of an FX plugin with current values and ranges. Supports filtering by name pattern, changed-only filter, and pagination. For a quick summary of active EQ bands or compressor settings, use analyze_fx instead.

fxIndex.description: Zero-based FX index in the chain

namePattern.description: Filter params by name (case-insensitive substring match, e.g. "Gain", "Band 1")

changedOnly.description: Only return params that appear non-default (value differs from minimum or formatted value suggests activity)

tools.name: analyze_fx
tools.description: Analyze an FX plugin and return a compact summary: FX name, preset, and notable (non-default) parameters. For EQ plugins, detects active bands with frequency/gain/Q/shape. For compressors, extracts threshold/ratio/attack/release/makeup. Use this before get_fx_parameters to understand what a plugin is doing without reading 500+ parameters.

fxIndex.description: Zero-based FX index in the chain

tools.name: set_fx_parameter
tools.description: Set a specific FX parameter value (normalized 0.0–1.0 for most plugins; use the parameter maxValue from get_fx_parameters when it is above 1)

fxIndex.description: Zero-based FX index in the chain

value.description: Parameter value: normalized 0.0–1.0 for most plugins; a few use their own range (ReaComp Threshold/Wet/Dry 0–2 linear gain, JSFX raw slider values). Check minValue/maxValue from get_fx_parameters

tools.name: set_fx_enabled
tools.description: Enable or disable (bypass) an FX plugin on a track

fxIndex.description: Zero-based FX index in the chain

tools.name: set_fx_offline
tools.description: Set an FX plugin online or offline. Offline FX uses no CPU but preserves settings.

fxIndex.description: Zero-based FX index in the chain

tools.name: read_track_meters
tools.description: Read real-time peak and RMS levels (in dB) for a track. Returns L/R peak and RMS values.

tools.name: read_track_spectrum
tools.description: Read the real-time frequency spectrum of a track while audio plays. Auto-inserts the MCP Spectrum Analyzer JSFX if not present. Returns 1/3-octave bands (25 Hz-16 kHz, ~0.5 s smoothed), each with raw `db` and K-weighted `kDb` (the BS.1770 weighting LUFS uses). Judge on `kDb`, never `db` (raw levels overstate the lows and understate 2-5 kHz), and compare a band only with the same band on another track or a reference. Pre-fader (the analyzer sits in the track FX chain); each read is a ~0.5 s snapshot, so read several times. Raw FFT bins only with includeBins.

includeBins.description: Also return every raw FFT bin (large: fftSize/2 values)

tools.name: play
tools.description: Start playback in REAPER

tools.name: stop
tools.description: Stop playback/recording in REAPER

tools.name: record
tools.description: Start recording in REAPER. Refused when no track is armed (REAPER would open a dialog that blocks the bridge): arm the target tracks first with set_track_record

tools.name: get_transport_state
tools.description: Get current transport state: play/record/pause status, cursor positions, tempo, time signature

tools.name: set_cursor_position
tools.description: Move the edit cursor to a specific position in seconds from project start

position.description: Position in seconds from project start

tools.name: list_available_fx
tools.description: Enumerate all installed FX plugins in REAPER (VST, VST3, JS, CLAP, AU) with an optional category filter

tools.name: search_fx
tools.description: Search installed FX plugins by name (case-insensitive substring match)

query.description: Search term to match against FX plugin names

tools.name: get_fx_preset_list
tools.description: List all available presets for a specific FX plugin on a track. Reads names by loading each preset, then restores the FX state; a MIDI plugin (e.g. ReaControlMIDI) may send each preset's messages while listing. Lists over 256 (generic program slots) are not enumerated (truncated: true).

fxIndex.description: Zero-based FX index in the chain

tools.name: set_fx_preset
tools.description: Apply a named preset to an FX plugin on a track

fxIndex.description: Zero-based FX index in the chain

tools.name: snapshot_save
tools.description: Save the current mixer state as a named snapshot. Stored in .reaper-mcp/snapshots/ alongside the project file (falls back to global bridge dir for unsaved projects). By default captures ALL tracks' volumes, pans, mutes, solos, FX bypass/offline states, full FX parameter values, preset names, track names/colors, and send levels. Pass trackIndices to scope the snapshot to specific tracks (e.g. just the master bus for an A/B that never touches other tracks). Pass fullChunk (or rely on its default-on when scoped) to capture exact track state chunks, which faithfully reproduce each plugin's internal state on restore — including plugins whose tone is driven by internal snapshots (e.g. Helix Native) that parameter-value capture cannot reproduce. Response includes storageLocation, scoped, fullChunk, and tracksCaptured.

includeFxParams.description: Include FX parameter values in snapshot (default true). Only applies to non-chunk capture.

maxParamsPerFx.description: Max parameters to capture per FX plugin (default 500). Only applies to non-chunk capture.

trackIndices.description: Restrict the snapshot to these 0-based track indices. Omit to capture all tracks. Restoring a scoped snapshot only affects the listed tracks.

fullChunk.description: Capture exact track state chunks (complete FX internal state, e.g. Helix Native snapshots) instead of parameter values. Defaults to true when trackIndices is set, false otherwise (whole-project chunk snapshots are large).

tools.name: snapshot_restore
tools.description: Restore a previously saved mixer snapshot by name. Reads from .reaper-mcp/snapshots/ alongside the project file (falls back to global bridge dir for unsaved projects). For chunk-based snapshots (saved with fullChunk), restores each captured track exactly via its state chunk — reproducing complete FX internal state (incl. plugin internal snapshots like Helix Native) and affecting only the tracks the snapshot captured. For parameter-based snapshots, restores volumes, pans, mutes, solos, FX bypass states, and FX parameters (parameters only when the plugin name matches, to avoid applying wrong values).

name.description: Name of the snapshot to restore

restoreTrackMeta.description: Also restore track names and colors (default false)

restoreSendLevels.description: Restore send volume/pan/mute for existing sends (default true)

tools.name: snapshot_list
tools.description: List all saved mixer snapshots for the current project. Reads from .reaper-mcp/snapshots/ alongside the project file (falls back to global bridge dir for unsaved projects). Response includes storageLocation ("project" or "global").

tools.name: snapshot_delete
tools.description: Delete a named mixer snapshot. Removes the snapshot file from .reaper-mcp/snapshots/ alongside the project file (or global bridge dir for unsaved projects). This action is permanent and cannot be undone.

name.description: Name of the snapshot to delete

tools.name: snapshot_edit
tools.description: Rename a mixer snapshot and/or change its description. The saved mixer state is kept. A new name whose file belongs to another snapshot is refused.

name.description: Name of the snapshot to edit

newName.description: New name; omit to keep the name

description.description: New description; omit to keep it, "" clears it

tools.name: get_track_routing
tools.description: Get sends, receives, and parent/folder information for a track — useful for understanding bus structure

tools.name: add_send
tools.description: Send one track to another (a bus, a reverb return, or a sidechain input). For a sidechain use mode "pre-fx" and destChannel 3; the destination is widened to 4 channels if needed. Tracks reach the master through their master send (set_track_info masterSend), not through add_send. Returns the new send as get_track_routing reports it.

from.description: Track: 0-based index (-1 = master), exact name, "{GUID}", or "master". A digit string means a track name first, then the index.

to.description: Track: 0-based index (-1 = master), exact name, "{GUID}", or "master". A digit string means a track name first, then the index.

mode.description: post-fader (default for new sends), pre-fx (sidechain feeds, cue mixes), post-fx (pre-fader)

srcChannel.description: Source channels: first channel of a stereo pair, 1-based (1 = 1/2, 3 = 3/4 for a sidechain)

destChannel.description: Destination channels: first channel of a stereo pair, 1-based (1 = 1/2, 3 = 3/4 for a sidechain)

tools.name: add_hardware_output
tools.description: Route a track straight to an audio interface output (outputChannel is 1-based; mono uses one channel).

track.description: Track: 0-based index (-1 = master), exact name, "{GUID}", or "master". A digit string means a track name first, then the index.

mono.description: Use one output channel instead of a stereo pair

mode.description: post-fader (default for new sends), pre-fx (sidechain feeds, cue mixes), post-fx (pre-fader)

tools.name: set_send
tools.description: Change a send, receive or hardware output by its index (as get_track_routing reports it). Only the given fields change.

track.description: Track: 0-based index (-1 = master), exact name, "{GUID}", or "master". A digit string means a track name first, then the index.

category.description: send (default): the track's sends; receive: its receives (the same objects, seen from the other end); hardware: its hardware outputs

mode.description: post-fader (default for new sends), pre-fx (sidechain feeds, cue mixes), post-fx (pre-fader)

srcChannel.description: Source channels: first channel of a stereo pair, 1-based (1 = 1/2, 3 = 3/4 for a sidechain)

destChannel.description: Destination channels (sends and receives): first channel of a stereo pair, 1-based (1 = 1/2, 3 = 3/4 for a sidechain)

mono.description: Mono hardware output (applied together with outputChannel)

tools.name: remove_send
tools.description: Remove a send, receive or hardware output by its index. Removing a receive removes the other track's send.

track.description: Track: 0-based index (-1 = master), exact name, "{GUID}", or "master". A digit string means a track name first, then the index.

category.description: send (default): the track's sends; receive: its receives (the same objects, seen from the other end); hardware: its hardware outputs

tools.name: add_track
tools.description: Insert a new track (default: at the end). Returns its index, name and GUID.

index.description: 0-based position to insert at (default: after the last track)

tools.name: delete_track
tools.description: Delete a track with its items, FX and routing (undoable with Ctrl+Z). The master track cannot be deleted. Later tracks move up one index.

track.description: Track: 0-based index (-1 = master), exact name, "{GUID}", or "master". A digit string means a track name first, then the index.

tools.name: move_track
tools.description: Move a track to a new 0-based position; the other tracks shift around it. The user's track selection is kept.

track.description: Track: 0-based index (-1 = master), exact name, "{GUID}", or "master". A digit string means a track name first, then the index.

toIndex.description: 0-based position the track ends up at

tools.name: set_track_folder
tools.description: Make a track a folder parent, the last track of a folder, or a normal track; optionally collapse the folder. Folders nest by position: tracks after a folder parent belong to it until a track marked "last".

track.description: Track: 0-based index (-1 = master), exact name, "{GUID}", or "master". A digit string means a track name first, then the index.

mode.description: folder: opens a folder at this track; last: closes the innermost open folder here; normal: neither

depth.description: Raw I_FOLDERDEPTH instead of mode (1 opens a folder, -N closes N levels)

tools.name: set_track_info
tools.description: Rename, color, set the channel count, or switch the master/parent send of a track. Everything is validated before anything is written.

track.description: Track: 0-based index (-1 = master), exact name, "{GUID}", or "master". A digit string means a track name first, then the index.

color.description: "#RRGGBB", or "none" to clear the custom color

channels.description: Track channel count, even (4 lets the track receive a sidechain on 3/4)

masterSend.description: Send this track to the master/parent track

tools.name: set_track_group
tools.description: Put a track in (or take it out of) a REAPER track group with given roles. Roles: volume_lead/follow, vca_lead/follow, pan_lead/follow, mute_lead/follow, solo_lead/follow, recarm_lead/follow, polarity_lead/follow, automode_lead/follow. A VCA: one track vca_lead, the others vca_follow.

track.description: Track: 0-based index (-1 = master), exact name, "{GUID}", or "master". A digit string means a track name first, then the index.

enable.description: true (default) adds the roles; false removes them

tools.name: read_track_lufs
tools.description: Read ITU-R BS.1770 loudness data for a track. Auto-inserts the MCP LUFS Meter JSFX if not present. Returns integrated, short-term (3s), and momentary (400ms) LUFS plus true inter-sample peak levels. Audio must be playing to accumulate data. The meter sits in the track FX chain, so it reads pre-fader: add the track volume (dB) for its level in the mix. Compare tracks in LU against the mix bus over the same section.

targetLufs.description: The integrated loudness you are working to, in LUFS, from the task (e.g. -14 for streaming, -23 for EBU R128 broadcast). Optional; shown against the reading on the bridge page, never changes the measurement

tools.name: read_track_correlation
tools.description: Read stereo field correlation and M/S analysis for a track. Auto-inserts the MCP Correlation Meter JSFX if not present. Returns correlation coefficient (-1 to +1), stereo width, and mid/side levels. Audio must be playing to accumulate data.

tools.name: read_track_crest
tools.description: Read crest factor (peak-to-RMS ratio) for a track. Auto-inserts the MCP Crest Factor Meter JSFX if not present. Returns crest factor in dB (higher = more dynamic, lower = over-compressed), peak hold level, and RMS level. Audio must be playing to accumulate data.

tools.name: measure_tracks
tools.description: Play audio and collect analysis measurements (LUFS, crest factor, correlation, spectrum) for one or more tracks in a single call. Handles playback start/stop automatically. LUFS and spectrum (1/3-octave bands) support multi-track; crest/correlation use global gmem and are only reliable for single-track measurement. First call may be slower due to JSFX meter auto-insertion. Readings are pre-fader (meters sit in each track FX chain): add each track volume to compare tracks; a folder/bus reads its children post-fader. Use this to balance tracks in LU and compare spectra on `kDb`. Afterwards it removes the MCP meters on the measured tracks (also ones an earlier call left) unless keepMeters. A meter that received no audio (muted, frozen or silent track, nothing in range) is reported under errors, not as numbers. For whole-song, folder or master numbers without playback, prefer analyze_track_offline.

trackIndices.description: Track indices to measure (max 8; -1 = master track)

durationSeconds.description: How long to play for measurement (seconds)

startPosition.description: Project position to seek to before playing (seconds)

targetLufs.description: The integrated loudness you are working to, in LUFS, from the task (e.g. -14 for streaming, -23 for EBU R128 broadcast). Optional; shown against the reading on the bridge page, never changes the measurement

keepMeters.description: Leave the MCP meter JSFX on the tracks (default: remove them afterwards)

tools.name: create_midi_item
tools.description: Create an empty MIDI item on a track at a given time range (seconds). Use this before inserting notes.

startPosition.description: Start position in seconds from project start

endPosition.description: End position in seconds from project start

tools.name: list_midi_items
tools.description: List all MIDI items on a track with position, length, and note/CC counts. ccCount counts CC messages only; channelEventCount and channelEventCounts include pitch bend, program change and pressure events

tools.name: get_midi_notes
tools.description: Get MIDI notes in a MIDI item. Supports pagination with offset/limit for large items. For a high-level overview of a large MIDI item, use analyze_midi instead. Returns pitch (0-127, 60=C4), velocity (0-127), position and duration in beats from item start.

limit.description: Max notes to return (default all). Use with offset to paginate large items.

tools.name: analyze_midi
tools.description: Analyze a MIDI item and return summary statistics computed in REAPER. Much more efficient than get_midi_notes for large items. Returns per-pitch stats (count, velocity min/max/avg/stddev), velocity histogram, and machine gun detection (consecutive identical velocities). Use this first to understand the MIDI data before reading individual notes.

tools.name: insert_midi_note
tools.description: Insert a single MIDI note. Pitch: 0-127 (60=C4/Middle C, 48=C3, 72=C5). Velocity: 1-127 (64=medium, 100=strong, 127=max). Position/duration in beats from item start (1.0=quarter, 0.5=eighth, 0.25=sixteenth).

startPosition.description: Start position in beats from item start

tools.name: insert_midi_notes
tools.description: Batch insert multiple MIDI notes in a single call. Pass a native array of note objects. Each note: { pitch, velocity, startPosition, duration, channel? }. Positions/durations in beats from item start (1.0=quarter, 0.5=eighth).

startPosition.description: Start position in beats from item start

tools.name: edit_midi_note
tools.description: Edit an existing MIDI note by index. Only provided fields are changed. Positions/durations in beats from item start.

startPosition.description: New start position in beats from item start

tools.name: edit_midi_notes
tools.description: Batch edit multiple MIDI notes in a single call. Much more efficient than calling edit_midi_note repeatedly. Pass a native array of edit objects, each with noteIndex and any fields to change (pitch, velocity, startPosition, duration, channel). Only provided fields are changed.

startPosition.description: New start position in beats from item start

edits.description: Array of note edits to apply

tools.name: delete_midi_note
tools.description: Delete a MIDI note by index from a MIDI item

tools.name: get_midi_cc
tools.description: Get CC (continuous controller) events from a MIDI item. Optionally filter by CC number (e.g. 1=modulation, 7=volume, 10=pan, 11=expression, 64=sustain).

tools.name: insert_midi_cc
tools.description: Insert a CC (continuous controller) event. Common CC numbers: 1=modulation, 7=volume, 10=pan, 11=expression, 64=sustain, 74=filter cutoff.

position.description: Position in beats from item start

tools.name: delete_midi_cc
tools.description: Delete a CC event from a MIDI item by the ccIndex get_midi_cc returned. ccIndex counts every channel event (pitch bend, program change and pressure too), so CC indexes can skip numbers; only pass an index get_midi_cc listed

ccIndex.description: 0-based channel-event index to delete (ccIndex from get_midi_cc)

tools.name: get_midi_item_properties
tools.description: Get detailed properties of a MIDI item including position, length, note count, CC count (CC messages only), channel-event counts by type, mute state, and loop setting

tools.name: set_midi_item_properties
tools.description: Set MIDI item properties: position (seconds), length (seconds), mute, loop source

position.description: New position in seconds from project start

tools.name: send_midi_cc
tools.description: Send a MIDI CC (continuous controller) event in real-time to a track's MIDI output. Auto-inserts the MCP MIDI Emitter JSFX if not present. Common CC numbers: 1=modulation, 7=volume, 10=pan, 11=expression, 64=sustain, 74=filter cutoff.

tools.name: send_midi_pc
tools.description: Send a MIDI program change in real-time, optionally preceded by bank select (CC0 MSB + CC32 LSB). Auto-inserts the MCP MIDI Emitter JSFX if not present.

bankMsb.description: Bank select MSB (CC0, 0-127) — omit if no bank select needed

bankLsb.description: Bank select LSB (CC32, 0-127) — omit if no bank select needed

tools.name: send_midi_note
tools.description: Send a MIDI note-on in real-time to a track's MIDI output. If durationMs is provided, a note-off is automatically scheduled after that many milliseconds. Auto-inserts the MCP MIDI Emitter JSFX if not present.

durationMs.description: Note duration in milliseconds (≥1) — if provided, schedules an automatic note-off

tools.name: list_media_items
tools.description: List all media items on a track with position, length, name, volume, mute state, and whether it is MIDI or audio

tools.name: get_media_item_properties
tools.description: Get detailed properties of a media item: position, length, volume, fades, play rate, take info, source file

tools.name: set_media_item_properties
tools.description: Set media item properties: position (seconds), length (seconds), volume (dB), mute, fade in/out lengths, play rate

position.description: New position in seconds

volume.description: New volume in dB (0 = unity gain)

tools.name: set_media_items_properties
tools.description: Batch set properties on multiple media items in a single call. Much more efficient than calling set_media_item_properties repeatedly. Pass a native array of item objects, each with trackIndex, itemIndex, and any properties to change.

position.description: New position in seconds

volume.description: New volume in dB (0 = unity gain)

items.description: Array of item property updates to apply

tools.name: split_media_item

tools.name: run_plan
tools.description: Execute a multi-step edit as ONE bridge call in ONE undo block, all-or-nothing. Use instead of many sequential tool calls. Ops run in order: add_track, set_track, add_fx, set_fx_params, add_send, graft_fxchain (copy a source FX chain onto a track; sends are not copied), select_tracks, copy_items / insert_time / remove_time (as the arrange tools), and run_action (any REAPER action — usually after select_tracks; same safety rules as run_action; only run_action ops may follow a run_action). Target tracks by index, exact name, "{GUID}", or a "$ref" that an earlier add_track/add_fx bound with `as`. Every target is resolved before anything is written: an unknown or ambiguous track rejects the whole plan, and a failure mid-apply reverts it. Use dryRun to preview resolution and conflicts. Pass an idempotencyKey so a retried call is not applied twice.

tools.name: analyze_track_aesthetics
tools.description: Analyze the perceptual aesthetic quality of a track's audio using Meta's Audiobox Aesthetics model (CC-BY 4.0). Bounces the track to a temp WAV file (post-FX, post-fader) and runs 4-axis perceptual quality scoring: Production Quality (PQ), Production Complexity (PC), Content Enjoyment (CE), Content Usefulness (CU). Returns scores 0-10. The clip is normalized to normalizeLufs (default -18 LUFS) before scoring, so level differences between versions do not bias the scores (CE rises with level; PQ barely moves). PQ (and partly CU) judge mix changes; PC and CE mostly follow the arrangement, so only compare the same time range. Measured noise: re-rendering the same 30 s clip moves PQ by ~0.05, a 10 s clip by ~0.4; treat smaller differences as no change. Requires the Python sidecar (run: node dist/apps/reaper-mcp-server/main.js setup-sidecar).

tools.description: Measure the time offset and polarity of one track against a reference track (e.g. snare bottom vs snare top, kick sub vs kick in, overheads vs snare) by rendering both over the same range and cross-correlating them. A positive delayMs means the track arrives later than the reference, as both play now (the current playback offset and polarity are included). To align it, set_track_property playOffsetMs = suggestedPlayOffsetMs and phase = suggestedPhase (1 = inverted) on that track — absolute values that already account for the current settings, so re-measuring an aligned track suggests what it already has. Renders are post-FX (plugin latency is compensated). Pick a range where both tracks play the same hits; below correlation 0.3 no suggestion is made. Requires the Python sidecar.

tools.name: verify_edit
tools.description: Check the result of an edit you just made, since you cannot hear it: compare the edited track with the audio from before the edit and get a verdict per check. Compensated null: the delay (ms, + = later), gain (dB) and polarity between the two are estimated and removed, and the residual left (dB below the reference) says whether anything else changed (noise, a splice, a different waveform, a swapped stereo channel; it is relative to referenceRmsDb, so with a quiet reference the rounding noise of a 16-bit bounce can set it). Discontinuity: the largest sample-to-sample jump on any channel against the reference's own, with where it happens and which channel (a click or hard splice). Use expect 'identical' (default) for edits that should leave the sound alone apart from level, delay and polarity (alignment, gain, split, crossfade): the residual is judged ok/warn/fail. Use "changed" for EQ, compression and the like: the residual is reported without a verdict. Set timeScale to the stretch factor when the edit changed the timing: the waveform null is then skipped and only the click check runs. The reference is another track (e.g. a copy you kept) or an audio file of the same range from before the edit (a bounce), not an undo. Keep a reference track unmuted so it renders. Pitch, formant and transient checks are not included: they need a baseline per source. A passing result is evidence, not a replacement for listening. Requires the Python sidecar.

Hits are paginated (offset/limit). Use it to sync lighting, video cuts, markers or MIDI to a song; create_transient_automation writes the hits as envelope pulses directly. A file is read as-is (no stretch markers or play rate): for an item warped to the grid, pass its track instead. Requires the Python sidecar.

Values are raw envelope values (FX parameters 0..1, Pan -1..1). Create the envelope first with create_track_envelope (it returns envelopeIndex). By default the envelope's points in the range are replaced (replaceExisting). dryRun returns the points without writing. Use bands/minStrength/minGapMs to choose what the lights follow (e.g. bands ["low"], minStrength 0.6 for the kick accents). Requires the Python sidecar.

The item keeps its length (anchors at both ends); the item's existing stretch markers are replaced. Returns the timing offset before and after (avg/max ms). Requires the sidecar.

Audio between hits is stretched; anchors at both ends keep each double's length. strength < 1 moves hits only part of the way. protectConsonants moves high-band hits (s, t, k, sh) as a block, so the stretch lands in the vowel after them instead of smearing the consonant. dryRun returns the planned moves and writes nothing. Each double's existing stretch markers are replaced; a guide that has stretch markers is refused (its hits would not sit where its source says). Returns, per double, the timing offset before and after (avg/max ms against the guide). Works on the items' source files (take FX are ignored). Requires the sidecar. Not pitch correction.

tools.name: import_midi_file
tools.description: Import a Standard MIDI File (.mid/.midi, type 0 or 1, up to 5 MB and 20000 notes) as MIDI items, without REAPER's import dialog: notes and controllers of every file track merged into one item on trackIndex, or with newTracks each file track on a new track named after it, inserted at trackIndex. Placed at position (seconds) on the project grid; the file's tempo is reported, not applied (set it with set_project_tempo). Pitch bend, program changes, aftertouch and sysex are not imported; file.notImported counts them. One undo point.

trackIndex.description: Track to put the item on, or with newTracks where the new tracks are inserted

newTracks.description: One new named track per file track (default: merge onto trackIndex)

position.description: Project time in seconds where the file starts (default 0)

tools.name: detect_key
tools.description: Detect the musical key (e.g. "A minor") of a track or an audio file: from a track's MIDI notes (note time weighted by velocity, drums on channel 10 ignored) or, for audio, from its rendered chroma (Python sidecar). Returns the key, confidence 0..1 (how far it stands out from the next candidate that is not its relative key, scaled down for a flat profile and by how well the key fits — its correlation), the relative key, the top 3 alternatives with their correlation, and the 12-bin chroma (C first). Use it before writing parts, choosing a pitch-correction scale or a harmonizer key.

trackIndex.description: Track to analyze (-1 = master). Give this or path

path.description: Absolute path of an audio file to analyze instead (sidecar)

itemIndex.description: Only the time this media item covers on trackIndex (from list_media_items); instead of startTime/endTime. Audio renders the whole track over it

source.description: For a track: midi (its MIDI notes), audio (render it), auto (default: MIDI notes when it has any, else audio)

startTime.description: Start of the range in seconds (project time for a track, file time for a file; default 0)

endTime.description: End of the range in seconds (track audio default: start + 60 s; MIDI and file default: the end)

tools.name: detect_chords
tools.description: Detect the chords of a track, one media item or an audio file, one per bar (default) or beat: from MIDI notes (drums on channel 10 ignored; the lowest held note gives slash chords like C/E) or from rendered audio (Python sidecar chroma). Track bars and beats follow the project tempo map; a file uses `bpm` (bar 1 at startTime) or fixed windows. Returns the key, the progression ("Am F C G"), and chord spans (equal neighbours merged): start/end seconds, bar.beat, chord, root, quality (maj, min, 7, maj7, m7, sus2, sus4, dim, aug; the model also dim7, m7b5, 6, m6, 9, maj9, m9, mMaj7, 5, 11, 13), roman numeral in the key, bassMidi (a MIDI note for a bass line, E1-D#2) and a 0..1 fit; "N" = no chord. Paginated (offset/limit). Audio uses the chord model (lv-chordia, slash chords and sevenths from a full mix) when installed (setup-sidecar --with-chords), else chroma templates; `engine` picks. Use it before writing a bass line or other parts to existing guitars, keys or vocals.

trackIndex.description: Track to analyze (-1 = master, audio only). Give this or path

path.description: Absolute path of an audio file to analyze instead (sidecar)

itemIndex.description: Only the time this media item covers on trackIndex (from list_media_items); instead of startTime/endTime. Audio renders the whole track over it

source.description: For a track: midi (its MIDI notes), audio (render it), auto (default: MIDI notes when it has any, else audio)

per.description: One chord per bar (default) or per beat

engine.description: Audio: model (the chord model, setup-sidecar --with-chords; also renders a MIDI track), template (chroma templates), auto (default: the model when installed). MIDI notes always use templates

startTime.description: Start of the range in seconds (project time for a track, file time for a file; default 0)

endTime.description: End of the range in seconds (default: where the track's last item ends, the project end on the master, the file's end; max 900 s for audio)

bpm.description: File only: its tempo, so segments are bars/beats from startTime

beatsPerBar.description: File only, with bpm: beats per bar (default 4)

windowSeconds.description: File only, without bpm: one chord per this many seconds (default 2)

limit.description: Most chord spans to return (default 64, max 256)

tools.name: transcribe_voice_sketch
tools.description: Compose an editable musical draft from humming, singing, beatboxing, or a mixture. Local Python sidecar, no model download. Returns stable rounded BPM, sustained tempo changes, tentative key, separate monophonic melody and GM drum notes, repeated 4/4 drum patterns, and original file times. Timing snaps to a shared grid (default sixteenths); pitches snap to semitones, NOT to a guessed key. By default arrange:true adds a proposed intro/verse/chorus/outro, a kick/snare/hat groove using detected kick positions and hat accents, chord accompaniment, bass locked to the kicks, and the repeated detected melody. Those backing parts and sections are GENERATED, not recovered from the recording. No true audio source separation. arrange:false exports only the detected melody/percussion. key overrides accompaniment only, never retunes the melody. Experimental: drum labels and octaves need review; speech is not removed. Use startTime/endTime to isolate music. No REAPER changes. outputPath writes the FULL score as a type-1 .mid with tempo map and GM instruments. With soundfontPath also renders a sampled mix and separate 32-bit WAV instrument stems into <outputPath without .mid>-stems/. This optional preview needs the FluidSynth shared library and a user-supplied GM .sf2; no audio device or REAPER needed. Then use import_midi_file(newTracks:true) and assign instruments. That importer skips GM programs and does NOT apply the file tempo: use set_project_tempo/add_tempo_marker separately, or REAPER native MIDI import. Summary-first: note arrays default to 100 events per part; limit:0 returns only summaries. Export is never paginated. At most 120 seconds input, 64 bars output, 240 seconds for previews. Requires setup-sidecar (core only is enough).

path.description: Absolute path of a voice recording (MP3/WAV/FLAC/AIFF/OGG)

startTime.description: Start in file seconds (default 0); exclude spoken cues

endTime.description: End in file seconds (default end of file, max 120 seconds selected)

mode.description: auto: both layers, melody: humming only, drums: beatboxing only

bpm.description: Force one fixed tempo; use for short clips or half/double-time ambiguity

grid.description: Grid in quarter-note beats: 0.25 sixteenths, 0.5 eighths, 1/3 triplets

minNoteMs.description: Shortest stable pitched segment before quantization (default 80 ms)

tempoChangeThreshold.description: Minimum relative tempo change, persisting in two 4-second windows (default 0.2 = 20%)

arrange.description: Generate a full backing arrangement; false returns the raw detected sketch only

bars.description: Generated arrangement length in 4/4 bars (default 16); ignored with arrange:false

key.description: Optional accompaniment key, e.g. A minor or Eb major. Does not change detected melody

outputPath.description: Optional absolute .mid path to create. Parent folder must exist. Existing files are never overwritten

soundfontPath.description: Optional absolute GM .sf2 for real sampled mix + stems. Requires outputPath and local FluidSynth library

offset.description: Note offset, independently in each part

limit.description: Notes returned per part (default 100, 0 = summary only); export always includes all notes

tools.name: list_builtin_knowledge
tools.description: List the built-in (read-only, curated) mix knowledge: plugin records and mixing lessons. Without query: summaries (key, tags, preview) — filter plugins by tags such as "category::eq" or "fx::Pro-Q 3". With query: full-text search returning full bodies. Combine with the user's own LoreKit layer (user:: keys), which overrides these.

tags.description: List mode: return rows having ANY of these tags (e.g. ["category::compressor"])

query.description: Full-text search instead of a list (e.g. "drum bus attack")

limit.description: Max results (default 50 for list, 5 for search)

tools.name: get_builtin_knowledge
tools.description: Read one built-in (read-only) record by key: "plugins::<vendor>/<plugin>" (e.g. "plugins::fabfilter/pro-q-3") or "mixing-lessons::<slug>". Returns null when the built-in layer has no such record. The user's own "user::" record of the same name, if any, overrides it.
